title: The Open Window
focus: a story so convincing it becomes real

teacherSummary.text: Nervous Framton Nuttel visits the Sappletons for a rest cure. While waiting, fifteen-year-old Vera tells him her aunt keeps the French window open because her husband and brothers vanished in a bog three years ago and she expects them back. When the men appear at the window with a spaniel, Framton flees in terror. Vera calmly invents a new story to explain his flight. 'Romance at short notice was her speciality.'

segments.script: Published in 1914 in Beasts and Super-Beasts. Saki (H. H. Munro) satirized Edwardian country-house society. A short masterpiece of the twist ending; in Gale's Short Stories for Students vol. 1. Irony: Dramatic irony is withheld: the reader believes Vera as Framton does, so the twist catches both. Characterization: Vera, "a very self-possessed young lady of fifteen," invents with total composure; Framton is anxious, self-absorbed and easy prey. Structure: A story within a story: Vera's ghost tale inside the visit, and a second invented tale (about Framton and the dogs) at the end. Watch for the open window: the opening through which Vera's fiction and the real world meet.
